data.body_html:
Choosing between the Azimut 58 Flybridge and the Sunseeker Predator 74 for your Marbella charter is a question of style and priorities. Both depart from Puerto Banús, carry up to 12 guests, and deliver a premium day on the Mediterranean. But they differ in size, speed, layout, and price. This comparison breaks down the numbers so you can decide which fits your group best.

Azimut 58 Flybridge Overview

The Azimut 58 Flybridge measures 17.6 metres and can accommodate 12 guests. Its flybridge layout offers a shaded upper deck with seating and sunbathing areas, perfect for panoramic views of the Costa del Sol coast. Cruising at 28 knots (top speed 32 knots), it balances comfort with performance. The interior features a spacious saloon and a well-equipped galley, while the aft deck leads to a swim platform for easy access to the sea. This boat is ideal for groups wanting a mix of relaxation and socialising.

Sunseeker Predator 74 Overview

The Sunseeker Predator 74 is longer at 22.5 metres and also takes 12 guests. Its open cockpit design emphasises a sportier feel, with a large sunpad aft and a sleek, aggressive profile. With a cruising speed of 30 knots and a top speed of 35 knots, it is the faster option. The interior is more compact than the Azimut's, but the outdoor spaces—especially the cockpit and bow sunpad—are designed for entertaining. This boat suits those who prioritise speed and open-air party vibes.

Size and Capacity Comparison

FeatureAzimut 58 FlybridgeSunseeker Predator 74
Length17.6 m22.5 m
Max Guests1212
Cabins3 (4 berths)3 (6 berths)
Heads22

The Predator is nearly 5 metres longer, offering more deck space but fewer berths per cabin. The Azimut's flybridge adds an entire social level that the Predator lacks.

Speed and Performance

Both boats are powered by twin diesel engines. The Azimut 58 reaches a top speed of 32 knots, while the Sunseeker Predator 74 tops out at 35 knots. For cruising, the Predator maintains 30 knots against the Azimut's 28 knots. The difference is noticeable if you plan to cover distance—say, from Puerto Banús to Cala del Faro or Estepona. The Predator can shave a few minutes off each leg, but both are fast enough for a comfortable day trip.

Layout and Onboard Experience

The Azimut 58 Flybridge shines with its upper deck, where guests can lounge on L-shaped seating, use a wet bar, and enjoy 360-degree views. The main deck has a saloon with large windows, a dining area, and a galley. The Sunseeker Predator 74 focuses on outdoor living: its cockpit has a large sunpad, a fold-down transom for swimming, and a forward sunpad on the bow. The interior is more streamlined, with a saloon and galley but less enclosed space.

Pricing and Charter Inclusions

Pricing for both boats is on request via WhatsApp. The Azimut 58 is generally more affordable than the larger Predator 74, but exact rates depend on season and duration. Both charters include a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish VAT (21%). You can book half-day (4 hours) or full-day (8 hours) trips.

Which One Should You Choose?

If you want a flybridge for lounging and socialising with panoramic views, the Azimut 58 Flybridge is the better choice. It offers more interior space and a relaxed vibe. If speed, open-air partying, and a sporty look matter more, the Sunseeker Predator 74 delivers. Both are excellent for groups of up to 12, departing from Puerto Banús. For a quieter day exploring coves like Cala Cortés or the coast toward Sotogrande, the Azimut suits. For a lively cruise with music and swimming stops, the Predator wins.

The Sunseeker Predator 74 is larger at 22.5 metres, compared to the Azimut 58 Flybridge at 17.6 metres. Both accommodate up to 12 guests, but the Predator offers more deck space and a longer hull.

Which boat is more luxurious?

Yes, every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish VAT (21%).

Both the Azimut 58 Flybridge and Sunseeker Predator 74 depart from Puerto Banús, Marbella's iconic marina.
